rounds.text: Bharti Telecom Ltd is severely under-appreciated by the market when examining its extraordinary return profile, led by a staggering Return on Equity of 64.7% and a median return on equity of 65% over the last year [E2, E5]. This superior capital efficiency is powerfully reinforced by a ROCE of 15.4% [E1]. Furthermore, the business is compounding its top line at 15% over the trailing twelve months, demonstrating robust underlying demand [E3]. Operational execution is equally exceptional, evidenced by an operating margin that surged to 54% in March 2025, marking a massive expansion of 19 percentage points against 35% three years earlier [E6]. This structural improvement is part of a sustained yearly operating-margin trend that has been increasing over the last four years [E7]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -1% [E4]. Despite this temporary profit contraction, the multi-year margin expansion and elite returns confirm a highly productive asset base that the current valuation fails to fully recognize [E2, E6, E7].

Conceded: [E6]. Despite the impressive optics of margin expansion, the fundamental engine of bottom-line wealth creation is stalling, as evidenced by a compounded profit growth of -1% over the trailing twelve months [E4]. This contraction in profits directly contradicts the narrative of robust fundamental health, suggesting that top-line expansion and margin gains are failing to translate into actual earnings growth [E3, E4, E6]. Furthermore, this operational disconnect is compounded by an inconsistent quarterly operating-margin trend over the last three quarters, exposing underlying volatility that higher annual averages tend to mask [E8]. While the return on equity sits at a lofty 64.7%, a negative profit growth rate raises serious questions about the sustainability and quality of those returns moving forward [E2, E4]. Investors are asked to pay up for high operating margins and returns on equity while actual profits shrink [E2, E4, E6].

The bear highlights a contraction in trailing twelve-month profit growth of -1% [E4], but this must be weighed against a robust top-line sales growth of 15% over the same period [E3]. Conceded: the quarterly operating-margin trend is inconsistent over the last three quarters [E8]. However, this short-term quarterly noise is decisively outweighed by the multi-year trajectory, where the yearly operating-margin trend has been steadily increasing over the last four years [E7]. This structural margin expansion is proven by a dramatic 19 percentage point surge in the operating margin to 54% in March 2025 compared to three years earlier [E6]. Consequently, the extraordinary 64.7% return on equity and 65% median return on equity are backed by genuine structural profitability gains rather than fleeting optics [E2, E5, E6].

Conceded: yearly operating-margin trend is increasing over the last four years [E7], and operating margin reached 54% in March 2025 which is a 19 percentage point increase against three years earlier [E6]. However, the bull's attempt to downplay profit growth of -1% as mere noise against 15% sales growth [E3, E4] ignores the fundamental disconnect between top-line expansion and actual bottom-line generation. Furthermore, while the bull dismisses the inconsistent quarterly operating-margin trend over the last three quarters [E8] as short-term noise, this volatility directly undermines the reliability of the headline 64.7% ROE and 65% median ROE [E2, E5]. When quarterly margins are inconsistent and trailing twelve-month profit growth actually contracts by -1% [E4, E8] despite robust sales [E3], the extraordinary equity returns [E2, E5] rely on an unstable foundation that the multi-year margin trend [E7] fails to guarantee on an ongoing basis.
